requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment:** the requirement is implemented completely and is tested, so I judge it satisfied.

**Implementation**

- **Initial set:** `AssessmentSources::prepare` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) builds the contributed selectors. These are the subject, its `{cite}`d requirements, the `{impl}` and `{test}` sources and the anchors. It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
- **Transitive closure:** `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies` (`src/terms.rs`).
  - `direct_references` scans the subject text and every contributed input. For Rust it scans only comments. For `Requirements` inputs it scans the declaration bodies. A directly supplied `Definition` input counts as a dependency.
  - `close_dependencies` expands to a fixed point over a `visited` set and a `BTreeSet`. That gives no duplicates and no nontermination on cycles. An unresolvable term or a malformed declaration is reported as an error.
- **Complete declaration:**
  - Each dependency becomes `InputSelector::Definition`, resolved by `source_input`. The resolved text is `target.raw_lines`, so it is the whole fenced declaration with its `:phrase:` option. The access policy is applied to the definition's file.
  - The result is deduplicated against the existing mandatory inputs (`!mandatory.contains`).
  - `initial_prompt` serialises all of `mandatory_inputs()` into the first request.
- **Additional reads:** the `read` tool (`habeas`) and the `search` tool (`ripgrep`) in `src/authoring/tools.rs` call `additional_definitions`. That recomputes the closure over the newly delivered inputs, with `subject = None`. It filters out definitions already in those inputs or already recorded, so there are no duplicates. Both tools return the definitions to the model and append them to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- **Recording:** `assess` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) holds delivered inputs in `pending` and calls `record_inputs` once the next provider response arrives. `record_inputs` deduplicates and keeps definition inputs in full. So tool-delivered definitions are supplied to the model, and recorded before a submission is accepted. If a provider request fails, `pending` is kept for the retry.
- **Marking:** the code that does this work carries `{impl}` markers for the requirement: `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `assess`, `read` and `search`. `terms::dependencies` is the shared closure code, and it is marked as implementing `requirements.definitions.dependencies`. I found no unmarked implementing code and no extra behaviour.

**Tests**

- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (`inputs.rs`):
  - The terms `unit` and `value` reference each other, which is a cycle.
  - It asserts exactly two definition inputs, so closure, deduplication and cycle termination are covered.
  - It also checks that definitions pulled in only through the other mandatory inputs (a cited requirement, impl and test sources) are included.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` (`inputs.rs`): a term referenced from an `{impl}` source comment is included in the mandatory set, and a definition file that is not staged is reported as an error.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (`mod.rs`):
  - A term referenced by a read source brings in a transitive, cyclic definition set.
  - The recorded evidence contains each definition exactly once, in order, as a full `:::{definition}` declaration with its `:phrase:` line.
  - The second request, the one that precedes the submission, carries the definitions; the first request does not.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` (`tools.rs`): the `habeas` and `ripgrep` tools supply and record the definitions. Repeated `record_inputs` calls do not duplicate. Error cases for invalid requests and unparseable files are covered.

**Remaining gaps:** none that matter. A dedicated test for an unresolvable term lives with the `requirements.definitions.dependencies` code and is outside this subject.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
